items.title: No Surprises Act IDR added $8.39B to health plan payment obligations: EBRI - BenefitsPRO
items.reason: This article directly addresses the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution process and its financial impact on health plans, which is a core component of NSA implementation relevant to revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: According to an Employee Benefit Research Institute (EBRI) analysis cited by BenefitsPRO, the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process has resulted in $8.39 billion in additional payment obligations imposed on health plans. This finding quantifies the financial impact of IDR determinations, where neutral arbitrators resolve disputes between providers and insurers over out-of-network emergency and certain non-emergency services. The result directly affects health plan cash flows and revenue-cycle teams' management of claim disputes under the NSA framework. For revenue-cycle professionals, this demonstrates the material financial consequences of IDR outcomes and underscores the importance of monitoring dispute resolution trends that influence payment obligations.
